title: Form and agreement gaps
summary: Infer tense, number, agreement, comparison and derived word forms from anchor words and the grammar controlling each gap.

sections.title: Keep the meaning, change the form
content: Say each family aloud: “meet, met”; “planter, planters”; “bright, brighter”; and “grow, growth”. The central meaning remains connected while grammar changes the required form.
A form gap often gives you the useful word somewhere nearby. Your job is to preserve its meaning while changing tense, number, agreement, degree or word class.

sections.title: Use the anchor–controller–form routine
content: Find the anchor: look for the same word, or a clearly related member of its word family, in the surrounding sentence or paragraph.

Find the controller: time expressions control tense; the subject controls verb and pronoun agreement; quantities control singular or plural number; comparison words control degree; and sentence position can require a noun, verb, adjective or adverb.
Build the form. Apply the smallest change that satisfies the controller, including an irregular form when necessary.
Reread the complete sentence and its neighbour. Check meaning, grammar and spelling before moving to the next gap.

sections.title: Let the controller decide the transformation
content: In “The club meets weekly. Last term, it ___ monthly”, the anchor is “meets” and “last term” requires the irregular past form “met”.
In “one planter … four more ___”, the quantity “four” requires the plural noun “planters”.
In “the roof is bright … became even ___ than before”, “than” signals a comparison, so “bright” becomes “brighter”.
In “the seedlings grew … their unexpected ___”, the determiner “their” and adjective “unexpected” create a noun position, so the verb “grew” supplies the related noun “growth”.

sections.title: Mark both pieces of evidence
content: For every gap, underline the anchor word and box the controller. Write a short label such as past, plural, third-person singular, past participle, comparative, noun or reflexive pronoun.
Test the completed phrase aloud. If it sounds possible but does not match the controller, revise the form rather than replacing it with an unrelated word.

sections.title: Complete a connected school report
content: Read all four paragraphs of “The rooftop garden record”. Supply one word for each of the eight gaps by transforming or matching an anchor already present in the passage.
Complete the whole passage before checking it. A later sentence may confirm whether a form refers to one person, several people, an earlier action or a comparison.

sections.title: Diagnose the form error
content: Gap role: I did not identify whether the gap required a verb, noun, comparison or pronoun.
Local grammar: I missed the time expression, subject, quantity, auxiliary or comparison word controlling the form.
Cohesion clue: I did not connect the gap to its anchor word or referent elsewhere in the passage.
Entry accuracy: I chose the correct form but misspelled it or entered an additional word. Record the closest cause before retrying.

sections.title: The rooftop garden record
content: Complete one original eight-gap passage covering irregular past tense, plural number, subject–verb agreement, a past participle, comparison, derivation and pronoun agreement. Feedback appears only after the full passage is submitted.
